questions.text: In the PDSA (Plan-Do-Study-Act) cycle, what is the primary purpose of the 'Study' phase?

options.a: To implement the improvement intervention on a large scale
options.b: To analyze results and determine whether the change led to improvement
options.c: To plan the next improvement project
options.d: To assign tasks to the improvement team

questions.explanation: The Study (or Check) phase involves analyzing the data collected during the Do phase to determine if the change produced the expected improvement, and identifying what was learned.

questions.text: A Pareto chart is used in quality improvement to:

options.a: Show the normal distribution of patient wait times
options.b: Identify the 'vital few' causes that account for the majority of problems
options.c: Map every step in a clinical process
options.d: Compare two groups of patients in a clinical trial

questions.explanation: A Pareto chart is a bar chart where causes are ordered by frequency. It applies the 80/20 rule — typically 80% of problems stem from 20% of causes — helping teams prioritize improvement efforts.

questions.text: Which Lean concept focuses on eliminating activities that do not add value from the patient's perspective?
questions.explanation: Muda is the Japanese term for waste. Lean methodology identifies seven types of waste (e.g., waiting, overproduction, defects) and focuses on eliminating activities that consume resources without adding value for the patient.

questions.text: A run chart that shows data points consistently above the median for eight or more consecutive points indicates:

options.b: A special cause signal suggesting a non-random shift in the process
options.c: The process is statistically out of control in both directions
options.d: The data collection method is incorrect

questions.explanation: Eight or more consecutive data points on the same side of the median is a run chart rule violation indicating special cause variation — a signal that something in the process has systematically changed.

questions.text: The Six Sigma methodology defines a process as 'in control' when the defect rate is:

options.b: No more than 3.4 defects per million opportunities
options.d: Below the industry average defect benchmark

questions.explanation: Six Sigma aims to achieve no more than 3.4 defects per million opportunities (DPMO), representing 99.99966% accuracy — a very high standard of process performance.
